messages.content:
You are an expert venture capital analyst evaluating crowdfunding projects. Compare the two project descriptions below along these criteria:
1. Clarity of value proposition
2. Market size and demand
3. Feasibility and development plan
4. Revenue model and sustainability
5. Differentiation
6. Impact and evidence plan
7. Risk awareness and mitigation

--- PROJECT A ---
## One-Sentence Summary

A software tool that scans real-world tools with a phone or webcam, auto-generates precisely scaled outlines, and exports ready-to-make files so users can design and produce custom organizers without CAD skills.

## Problem

The creators argue that organizing tools and parts is slow and technical, typically requiring CAD expertise, manual measurements, or specialized hardware. This creates friction for makers and shops who want custom-fit inserts or boards tailored to their own tools.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product combines a mobile scanner and a desktop web app: users place a tool on paper, capture an image from about 3 ft (1 m), and the software scales and traces the outline to exact dimensions. The desktop app syncs scans, lets users refine contours, add labels, and preview inserts, then exports manufacturing-ready files for 3D printing, laser cutting, milling, or ordering through in-app partners.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Phone-based scanning with automatic scaling to true size.

-   Browser-based editor that syncs with mobile; instant updates across devices.

-   Exports: STL, SVG, DXF, and STP for printing, cutting, or routing; option to order directly in-app.

-   "New features" highlighted: faster interface; one-click STL export; peg-board design; custom drawer outlines; public library of tool shapes and inserts; search by name; webcam scanning; ability to purchase tools in-app.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Intended for makers and professional environments such as machine shops and commercial toolboard manufacturers---anyone needing quick, custom storage solutions for drawers, boards, or cases.

## Development Status

The campaign presents a working concept with both phone and desktop components and details of the forthcoming "new app," implying an active development phase focused on speed, features, and workflow polish.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

The team is "aiming to deliver the new app by January 1st." Stretch goals include a custom organizer library (noted as grid-style trays and bins) and a desktop installation for offline use. The team plans to ship the core first---catalog, search, drawer layouts, and DXF/SVG export---then add extras afterward.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds are described as directly enabling dedicated build time; if full-time staffing is not possible, senior contractors will be engaged, acknowledging that progress may be slower.

## Risks & Challenges

Stated risks include staffing and scope management, scanning accuracy variations due to lighting or finishes, file-format compatibility across machines, platform updates, and service uptime. Mitigations include shipping a focused core, calibration and manual edit tools, exporting standard formats, testing against OS/browser betas, using trusted cloud services with backups, and maintaining a status page.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by founders with mechanical engineering and sustainable additive manufacturing/product design experience. The campaign references in-app ordering through partners and a search for sustainable manufacturing partners.

## What's Included

Access to the software, the ability to scan and sync on mobile/desktop, editing and labeling tools, and exports in STL/SVG/DXF/STP; a public library of shapes and inserts is also described.

## Technical Details

-   Phone capture distance: \~3 ft (1 m).

-   Outputs: STL, SVG, DXF, STP.

-   Works via phone camera, webcam, and a browser-based desktop app; includes calibration and manual edits.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team plans hotfixes for platform changes, a status page for outages, and community features where users can browse shared projects and shapes. The campaign notes some source code may be updated using AI-generated code.
--- END PROJECT A ---

--- PROJECT B ---
## One-Sentence Summary
A privacy-first platform that creates permanent, verifiable digital fingerprints of ethical sourcing events anchored to a public, tamper-proof ledger, building an educational ecosystem for supply chain professionals, NGOs, and philanthropic foundations to independently verify provenance and substantiate impact.

## Problem
The venture plans to address a digital landscape saturated with manipulation and duplication, where it is increasingly difficult to establish what is original or real. The central challenge is enabling people to credibly prove the authenticity and first possession of a digital record—such as a donation confirmation or an impact report—amid pervasive skepticism and the ease of generating false claims. A specific, related challenge the venture plans to explore as the primary focus for its initial development is the inefficiency and lack of standardization in the verification process for corporate matching gift programs, where employees often face cumbersome manual steps to prove their donations, creating friction that reduces participation.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The venture plans to initially target a single, concrete user group for its MVP: employees at companies with corporate matching gift programs, who need a streamlined, trustworthy way to submit donation receipts for verification and matching. This initial use case is planned to serve as the primary focus for product development and user testing. The venture plans to explore targeting other groups, such as procurement teams within consumer goods companies and NGOs, in subsequent phases.

## Solution / Product Overview
The venture plans to build a tool initially focused on streamlining verification for corporate matching gift programs. To ensure the proposed tool's 'compact fingerprint' effectively captures the necessary information for verification, the venture plans to conduct a focused analysis of 3-5 existing corporate matching gift program guidelines to identify common required data fields. This planned review is intended to directly inform the fingerprint's design. Furthermore, before building the MVP, the venture plans to propose a small, targeted test with 3-5 employees from different companies to gather qualitative feedback on the user experience of creating a digital fingerprint. This test is planned to provide early insights into usability and clarity. The venture also plans to propose a small, targeted test with 3-5 employees to gather qualitative feedback on the perceived trust and credibility of the digital fingerprint versus a traditional receipt, specifically focusing on their comfort level in submitting it to their employer. The proposed tool would then allow an employee to create a digital fingerprint of their donation receipt and record proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is proposed to be secure and privacy-preserving: users would not upload sensitive raw data; instead, a compact fingerprint would serve as durable evidence for the corporate matching program administrator. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that donors and verifying corporate partners can rely on. To increase trust, the team plans to explore adding a decentralized, community-run witness network to provide a secondary, distributed layer of attestation to the ledger's timestamps. Furthermore, the venture plans to explore the development of a simple, open-source verification widget that any third-party website (like a corporate social responsibility page) could embed to allow administrators to independently verify the timestamp and authenticity of a claimed donation fingerprint directly. Before developing this widget, the venture plans to propose a small, targeted test with 3-5 corporate matching gift program administrators to gather qualitative feedback on the widget's proposed interface and clarity. The venture also plans to explore adding a simple, optional feature for the MVP where an employee can generate a shareable verification link for their donation fingerprint, aiming to increase transparency and user control. To demonstrate the efficiency gains of its initial MVP, the venture plans to track a specific, simple metric: the average time required for a corporate administrator to verify a single submitted donation receipt, from receipt of the employee's claim to confirmation of its validity. As a planned next step for validating this metric, the venture plans to propose a targeted, small-scale test before any planned pilot. This test would involve manually simulating the verification process with 5-10 donation receipts from volunteers to establish a baseline and refine the approach. Following this, the venture plans to propose a small-scale pilot test with a single corporate partner to validate the metric of average verification time reduction. The venture plans to explore a partnership with a single matching gift platform (e.g., Benevity, CyberGrants) for this planned pilot, framing it as a test of integration feasibility and potential distribution channel.

## Delivery Model
The venture plans a lightweight, privacy-first implementation for this initial use case. It would not store sensitive donor financial details or the underlying receipt files. Instead, it would generate compact, anonymized fingerprints of that data for ledger anchoring. The goal is a secure and resource-conscious design that maintains long-term verifiability with minimal infrastructure. The team plans to build a clean public interface and supporting infrastructure to make the verification tools usable by employees and corporate administrators.

## Revenue Logic
The venture plans to generate revenue through the sale of a subscription service to corporations for access to the verification ledger and streamlined matching gift program management capabilities. An initial free trial period for the subscription service is proposed to onboard corporate partners. The venture also plans to explore potential optional upgrades for enhanced connectivity or integration services for enterprise HR or philanthropy programs, building from this initial use case. To validate the demand and willingness-to-pay for this subscription model, the venture plans to propose a small, targeted test involving informal interviews with 3-5 potential corporate administrators where the proposed pricing model would be simulated and discussed.

## Distinctiveness
The venture aims to differentiate its initial offering by focusing on solving the specific credibility and friction problem in corporate matching gift verification. Its proposed system does not just provide a submission portal; it aims to create a permanent, independently verifiable record that a donation was made at a specific time, addressing the administrative burden and skepticism in current processes. This focus on verifiable proof for a specific, high-friction corporate social responsibility workflow is presented as a unique safeguard for both employee trust and program efficiency. The venture plans to explore a further point of differentiation: structuring its public ledger not just as a tamper-proof record for receipts, but as a machine-readable, open registry of verified charitable actions. To make the semantic clarity claim more tangible in early discussions, the venture plans to explore adding a single, simple example of a 'machine-readable' program rule (e.g., 'donation must be to a 501(c)(3) organization') to the planned open registry concept. This would allow the fingerprints to be programmatically linked to the precise definitions of the matching program rules, aiming to create a new layer of semantic clarity and auditability that is missing from current manual verification.
--- END PROJECT B ---

For each project, list its pros and cons as bullet points (use "•" as the bullet marker), grounded in the criteria above. Do not reward unsupported specificity: claims of traction, partnerships, testimonials, completed development, or quantified evidence should improve a project's assessment only when they are genuine source facts. Then state which project wins overall and why.

Respond with a JSON object: {"analysis": "your analysis here", "winner": "A" or "B"}
Output only valid JSON, nothing else.
